title: Microfossils Help Crack Mystery More Than 100 Million Years in the Making
gist: A new Science study links the breakup of Gondwana — and the violent Indian Ocean hot-spot volcanism it unleashed — to the second-largest extinction of planktic foraminifera, 113 million years ago in the early Cretaceous. The fossil record shows the microorganisms building progressively smaller, thinner calcium carbonate shells before vanishing.

insights.claim: A study published in Science attributes a massive early Cretaceous oceanic extinction event to the fallout from the breakup of the supercontinent Gondwana, which began around 180-160 million years ago and was marked by violent volcanic activity in newly formed Indian Ocean hot spots.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Tectonic-scale volcanism is being formalized as a driver of ocean chemistry collapse — the deep-time analog for how fast carbon injection reshapes marine carbonate systems.
insights.quote: Now a new study published today in Science blames the fallout from that breakup for a massive oceanic extinction event.
insights.locator: No matter how bad your breakup

themes.theme: Shell thinning as a pre-collapse signal

insights.claim: Planktic foraminifera — microscopic organisms with calcium carbonate shells living in shallow ocean waters — suffered their second largest extinction event 113 million years ago during the early Cretaceous.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Calcifying plankton are the base of the marine carbon pump; their historical failure points mark thresholds worth watching in modern ocean-acidification work.
insights.locator: During the early Cretaceous period 113 million years ago

insights.claim: Before disappearing, planktic foraminifera left a fossil record of progressively smaller and thinner shells, and unlike the abrupt end-Cretaceous event that eliminated the dinosaurs this die-off was much more gradual.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Gradual morphological degradation ahead of collapse is a leading-indicator pattern: the system telegraphs stress long before the endpoint.
insights.quote: the fossil record shows planktic foraminifera building smaller, thinner shells before they vanished
